title: AWS S3 → Google Cloud Storage: 15 TB Production Migration
description: Designed and implemented a production-grade cross-cloud migration strategy to move approximately 15 TB of object data from Amazon S3 to Google Cloud Storage with minimal application disruption. The migration focused on data integrity, minimal downtime, incremental synchronization, secure cross-cloud access, automated validation, monitoring, failure handling and rollback capability.
executive_summary: Designed and implemented a production-grade migration strategy to move approximately 15 TB of object data from Amazon S3 to Google Cloud Storage while minimizing application disruption. The migration architecture was designed around controlled bulk transfer, incremental synchronization, automated reconciliation, secure cross-cloud access, production cutover validation and rollback capability.
features: AWS S3 to Google Cloud Storage migration
Managed bulk transfer using Google Cloud Storage Transfer Service
Incremental synchronization for continuously changing production data
Checksum and integrity validation where available
Rollback capability using the original S3 source
Encryption in transit and at rest
Sanitized infrastructure and validation reference implementation

architecture.overview: The migration architecture uses Google Cloud Storage Transfer Service as the managed data movement layer between the AWS S3 source and Google Cloud Storage destination. The source environment remains available throughout the migration to support incremental synchronization, validation and rollback.
data_flow: Production objects are stored in AWS S3
Storage Transfer Service performs the initial bulk transfer
Transferred objects are written to Google Cloud Storage
Application continues operating against the source during migration
Incremental synchronization transfers newly created or changed objects
Final synchronization is performed during the controlled cutover window
Application configuration is switched to Google Cloud Storage
AWS S3 is retained during the rollback window

migration_strategy.description: The migration was divided into discovery, initial transfer, incremental synchronization, validation and controlled production cutover phases.

phases.objective: Establish a reliable baseline before transferring production data.
activities: Analyze application read and write patterns

phases.objective: Perform the initial bulk transfer of approximately 15 TB.
activities: Retain source S3 data during transfer

phases.objective: Synchronize changes created or modified after the initial transfer.
activities: Allow production application to continue operating against S3
Identify objects changed after the initial migration

phases.objective: Verify that the destination accurately represents the production source before application cutover.
Move application traffic to Google Cloud Storage with minimal downtime.
activities: Keep AWS S3 available for rollback

data_validation.description: Validation is performed at multiple levels to ensure that the destination contains the expected production data before cutover.

validation_levels.method: Compare the total number of objects in S3 with the total number of objects in GCS.
Compare the total number of bytes stored in S3 with the total number of bytes stored in GCS.
Compare object names and sizes between the source and destination and validate checksums where supported.
validation_levels.expected_result: Missing objects = 0, extra objects = 0, size mismatches = 0, checksum mismatches = 0 where applicable

cutover.description: Production cutover is performed only after the final synchronization and validation checks have completed successfully.

rollback_strategy.description: The original AWS S3 source is retained during the defined rollback window to avoid making the migration irreversible before application validation is complete.
rollback_flow: Application is pointed back to AWS S3
Application health and data access are validated
Migration issue is investigated before another cutover attempt

security.description: The migration was designed around least-privilege access and avoiding long-lived credentials in source control.

migration_identity: AWS S3: Required list and read permissions only
Google Cloud Storage: Required destination write permissions only

observability.description: Migration progress and operational health are monitored throughout the transfer and validation lifecycle.

failure_handling.response: Retry the object transfer and investigate persistent failures.
Validate AWS IAM and Google Cloud IAM permissions and confirm least-privilege access requirements.
Review destination capacity and applicable Google Cloud quotas.
Use managed transfer retry mechanisms and investigate persistent failures.
Identify affected objects and perform targeted reconciliation or retransmission.
Execute the rollback procedure and restore application access to AWS S3.
Do not complete production cutover until the discrepancy is resolved.

engineering_decisions.decision: Use Google Cloud Storage Transfer Service
engineering_decisions.reason: A managed transfer service reduces the operational overhead of maintaining custom transfer infrastructure and provides transfer orchestration, retries, monitoring and integrity handling.
Keeping the source available provides a rollback path and prevents an irreversible migration decision before application and data validation are complete.
Production data may continue changing after the initial bulk transfer, so incremental synchronization is required to capture changes before cutover.
Object count and total size alone do not provide sufficient assurance that every object has been migrated correctly.
Quiescing application writes during the final synchronization reduces the risk of data divergence during the transition.
Cloud-native IAM and secret management reduce credential exposure and support stronger security controls.

why_storage_transfer_service.reason: For a large production cross-cloud migration, a managed transfer service provides transfer orchestration, scheduling, retry handling, operational visibility and reduced infrastructure management compared with building and maintaining a fleet of custom transfer workers.

why_not_simple_cli_sync.decision: Avoid relying solely on a basic CLI synchronization process
why_not_simple_cli_sync.reason: A CLI-based synchronization approach can be useful for smaller workloads, but a production-scale 15 TB migration benefits from managed transfer orchestration, better operational visibility, retry handling, scheduling, reconciliation and reduced operational overhead.

lessons_learned: Large-scale data migration is primarily a data integrity and operational risk problem rather than simply a file-copy problem.
Object count and total bytes alone are insufficient for strong migration validation.
Production writes must be explicitly handled throughout the migration lifecycle.
Final synchronization and application cutover require a controlled change window.
Source data should not be deleted immediately after migration.
Least-privilege cross-cloud access is critical for secure migration operations.
Large numbers of small objects can behave differently from a small number of large objects during large-scale transfer.
Migration monitoring and reconciliation should be automated rather than performed manually.
Rollback planning should be part of the migration design before production cutover.
Data validation should be treated as a first-class migration phase rather than an afterthought.
operational_workflow: Analyze object distribution and application access patterns
Quiesce application writes during final cutover
Perform object count and byte reconciliation
Retain S3 for the defined rollback window
Decommission source resources only after migration acceptance
portfolio_highlights: Designed a 15 TB production-scale cross-cloud object storage migration.
Implemented a controlled AWS S3 to Google Cloud Storage migration strategy.
Used managed Google Cloud Storage Transfer Service for bulk and incremental transfer.
Designed multi-level data validation and reconciliation.
Implemented object count, byte-level and checksum-based validation where available.
Designed a production cutover process with minimal downtime.
Maintained AWS S3 as a rollback source during the migration window.
Applied least-privilege AWS and Google Cloud IAM principles.
Designed migration monitoring, failure handling and retry workflows.
Automated infrastructure and validation components using Terraform, Python and Bash.
challenges: Migrating approximately 15 TB of production object data between cloud providers while maintaining data integrity and minimizing application disruption. The major challenges included handling continuously changing source data, performing reliable object-level reconciliation, controlling cross-cloud permissions, managing transfer failures, coordinating final synchronization and maintaining a safe rollback path.
solution: Used Google Cloud Storage Transfer Service for the initial bulk migration and incremental synchronization, retained AWS S3 as the source of truth during the migration window, implemented multi-level validation using object counts, total bytes, object metadata and checksums where available, and performed a controlled final synchronization and application cutover only after validation succeeded. Cross-cloud access was secured through least-privilege IAM permissions, while monitoring and failure-handling mechanisms provided operational visibility throughout the migration.
